stem.en: Which plasma protein is mainly responsible for maintaining osmotic balance?

explanation.en: Fibrinogen helps clotting, globulins help defence and albumins maintain osmotic balance. Haemoglobin is in RBCs, not plasma.

stem.en: The most abundant leucocytes in human blood are:

explanation.en: Neutrophils form 60–65% of the total WBCs.

stem.en: Which leucocytes secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin?

explanation.en: Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin and are involved in inflammatory reactions.

stem.en: Which statement about human erythrocytes is correct?

options.en: They are formed in the spleen in adults
They have an average life span of 120 days and are destroyed in the spleen

explanation.en: RBCs are anucleate, biconcave, formed in red bone marrow, number 5–5.5 million per mm³, live about 120 days and are destroyed in the spleen.

stem.en: A person with blood group AB has:

options.en: antigens A and B on RBCs and no anti-A or anti-B antibodies

explanation.en: AB individuals have both antigens and neither antibody, so they are universal recipients.

stem.en: In the clotting cascade, thrombin converts:

explanation.en: Thrombokinase converts prothrombin to thrombin; thrombin converts soluble fibrinogen to insoluble fibrin.

stem.en: Erythroblastosis foetalis can occur when:

options.en: an Rh+ mother carries an Rh− foetus
both mother and foetus are Rh−
the mother has blood group O and the father blood group AB
an Rh− mother carries an Rh+ foetus in a later pregnancy

explanation.en: The Rh− mother gets sensitised to Rh antigen during the first delivery; anti-Rh antibodies can destroy foetal RBCs in later pregnancies.

stem.en: Which statement about lymph is correct?

options.en: It contains RBCs and platelets in large numbers
It contains specialised lymphocytes and carries absorbed fats from the intestine
It flows from veins into capillaries
It has a mineral distribution very different from plasma

explanation.en: Lymph has the same mineral distribution as plasma, contains lymphocytes, drains into major veins and carries fats absorbed through lacteals.

stem.en: Which of the following animals has a 4-chambered heart?

explanation.en: Crocodiles, birds and mammals have 4-chambered hearts; amphibians and other reptiles have 3; fishes have 2.

stem.en: The opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle is guarded by the:

explanation.en: The bicuspid or mitral valve guards the left atrio-ventricular opening; the tricuspid guards the right.

stem.en: The pacemaker of the human heart is the:

explanation.en: The SAN generates the maximum number of action potentials (70–75/min) and sets the rhythm.

stem.en: The atrio-ventricular node is located in the:

options.en: right upper corner of the right atrium
lower left corner of the right atrium, close to the AV septum

explanation.en: NCERT: the AVN lies in the lower left corner of the right atrium close to the atrio-ventricular septum; the SAN is in the right upper corner of the right atrium.

stem.en: The first heart sound "lub" is produced by the closure of the:

explanation.en: Lub is due to closure of the AV (tricuspid and bicuspid) valves; dub is due to closure of the semilunar valves.

stem.en: In an ECG, the QRS complex represents:

explanation.en: P = atrial depolarisation, QRS = ventricular depolarisation, T = ventricular repolarisation.

stem.en: If the stroke volume is 70 mL and the heart rate is 72 per minute, the cardiac output is about:

explanation.en: Cardiac output = 70 mL × 72 = 5040 mL ≈ 5 L/min.

stem.en: A person's heart rate is 75 beats per minute. The duration of one cardiac cycle is:

explanation.en: Duration = 60 ÷ 75 = 0.8 s.

stem.en: The hepatic portal vein carries blood from the:

explanation.en: The hepatic portal system carries blood from the intestine to the liver before it enters systemic circulation.

stem.en: Which of the following increases the heart rate?

explanation.en: Sympathetic nerves increase the rate and strength of heartbeat; parasympathetic signals decrease them.

stem.en: Acute chest pain that appears when not enough oxygen reaches the heart muscle is called:

explanation.en: Angina pectoris is acute chest pain due to insufficient O2 reaching the heart muscle.

stem.en: Which statement correctly distinguishes heart failure from cardiac arrest?

options.en: Both mean that the heart stops beating
In heart failure the heart pumps ineffectively; in cardiac arrest it stops beating
Heart failure is sudden muscle damage; cardiac arrest is chest pain
In cardiac arrest the lungs are congested; in heart failure the heart stops

explanation.en: Heart failure (congestive) = ineffective pumping with lung congestion; cardiac arrest = heart stops; heart attack = heart muscle suddenly damaged by inadequate blood supply.

passage.en: A patient with blood group B is rushed into the emergency ward and needs a transfusion. The blood bank has units from four donors: P (group A), Q (group AB), R (group O) and S (group B). The technician must avoid any donor whose red cells carry an antigen against which the patient's plasma has antibodies.

stem.en: From which donors can the patient safely receive blood?

explanation.en: A group B person has antigen B and anti-A antibodies in plasma, so cells carrying antigen A (groups A and AB) would be attacked. Group B (S) and group O (R), which has no antigens, are safe.

passage.en: An Rh-negative woman is expecting her second child. Her husband is Rh-positive, and their first child was Rh-positive. After the first delivery she was not given anti-Rh antibodies. Her doctor now orders regular checks of the fetus's blood.

stem.en: If the second fetus is also Rh-positive, what is the doctor's main worry?

options.en: The mother's anti-Rh antibodies, formed after the first delivery, may cross the placenta and destroy the fetal RBCs (erythroblastosis foetalis).
The fetus will make antibodies that destroy the mother's RBCs.
The fetus will develop blood group O.
There is no risk, because the Rh antigen never meets the mother's blood.

explanation.en: During the first delivery the mother can be exposed to Rh antigens of the fetus and make anti-Rh antibodies. In a later Rh-positive pregnancy these can leak into the fetal blood and destroy its RBCs, causing severe anaemia and jaundice (erythroblastosis foetalis).

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The sino-atrial node (SAN) is called the pacemaker of the heart.
Reason (R): The SAN can generate the maximum number of action potentials, 70–75 per minute, and so initiates and maintains the rhythm of the heart.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true; because the SAN generates the most action potentials per minute, it sets the rhythm, which is why it is the pacemaker.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The QRS complex in a standard ECG represents the repolarisation of the ventricles.
Reason (R): The T-wave represents the return of the ventricles from the excited to the normal state.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is false: the QRS complex represents depolarisation of the ventricles, which starts ventricular contraction. R is true: the T-wave represents ventricular repolarisation.

stem.en:
Match Column I with Column II.
I: (a) Neutrophils (b) Basophils (c) Eosinophils (d) Lymphocytes
II: (i) associated with allergic reactions (ii) immune responses (B and T cells) (iii) phagocytosis of foreign organisms (iv) secrete histamine, serotonin, heparin

explanation.en: Neutrophils are phagocytic, basophils secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin, eosinophils are linked to allergy, and lymphocytes (B and T) give immune responses.

stem.en:
Read the statements:
I. The RBC count of a healthy adult is 5 to 5.5 million per mm³.
II. RBCs live about 120 days and are destroyed in the spleen.
III. Platelets are cell fragments produced from megakaryocytes.
IV. Plasma forms about 45 per cent of the blood.
Which of these are correct?

explanation.en: Plasma forms nearly 55 per cent of blood; formed elements form about 45 per cent. The other three statements are correct.

stem.en:
Match the parts of a standard ECG with what they represent.
I: (a) P wave (b) QRS complex (c) T wave (d) End of the T wave
II: (i) end of systole (ii) depolarisation of the atria (iii) repolarisation of the ventricles (iv) depolarisation of the ventricles

explanation.en: P = atrial depolarisation, QRS = ventricular depolarisation, T = ventricular repolarisation; the end of the T wave marks the end of systole.

stem.en: An ECG strip shows 20 QRS complexes in 15 seconds. If the stroke volume is 70 mL, the heart rate and cardiac output are:

explanation.en: Heart rate = 20 × (60/15) = 80 per minute (one cycle 0.75 s). Cardiac output = 80 × 70 mL = 5600 mL ≈ 5.6 L/min.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The ventricles fill with blood even before the atria contract.
Reason (R): During joint diastole the tricuspid and bicuspid valves are open, so blood flows from the atria into the ventricles.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: During joint diastole the AV valves are open and blood flows into the ventricles; atrial systole then adds only about 30 per cent more.
